Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed opacity occupying the lower half of the right hemithorax, which obscures the right hemidiaphragm and cardiac border. Given its significant size and mass effect in an asymptomatic patient, this appearance is characteristic of a giant solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura, for which surgical resection is the standard management to relieve compression and rule out malignancy.
